segments.he: מוהרנ"ת ז"ל אמר שהעולם אומרים שאם אוכלים חזיר עכ"פ יאכלו כ"כ שיזל על הזקן (אז מען עסט חזיר זאל חטאשי רינען איבער דער בארד) ואני אומר שאם אוכלין חזיר עכ"פ אל יזל על הזקן (אז מען עסט שון חזיר זאל חאטשי ניט רינין איבער דער בארד) היינו שיאכלו עכ"פ מעט. (פי' שהעולם אומרים כיון שעושים עבירה להנות ממנה יעשהו עכ"פ כיון שכבר עושים עכ"פ יעשה שיהנו הרבה. זאל חטאשי ניט זיין אומזיסט. ומהרנ"ת אמר אפי' כשעושים ח"ו עבירה עכ"פ כמה שאכל למעט ומעט כי הכל בחשבון גדול וכו').
segments.en:
Reb Natan's custom during the Three Weeks was to recite the kinos [lamentations] with tallis and tefillin. And he would say Tikkun Chatzos at noon in a deep cellar — weeping and pouring out his heart until nightfall.

And Reb Nachman of Tulchin on Tisha B'Av — at night and through the day until midday — would not speak a single word with any person, and would not study Midrash with the congregation as was the custom of the day.

And the holy Rav of Berdichev would wear his shtreiml on Erev Tisha B'Av — and wait and hope, near the time of nightfall, that Mashiach would come so that he could go out to greet him.

I heard that after Rabbainu's passing, on the first Shabbos, the disciples of Rabbainu gathered in Rabbainu's house. Reb Yudel said he would sit in Rabbainu's chair — because he had inherited Rabbainu's shtreiml. Then Moharan'as arose and said that he had inherited the mochin [higher mind] of Rabbainu — for tefillin is mochin, and Rabbainu had intentionally put on Moharan'as's tefillin so that Moharan'as would receive his mochin. And Moharan'as then sang the melody of Azamer Bishvachin with great arousal — and the holy Magid of Terhovitsa leaped from the table and said: "I thought it was Reb Noson — but now I see it is Rabbainu himself!"

And the essential root of the controversy of the Rabbi of Savran against Reb Noson was that Moharan'as bound himself with great self-sacrifice so that the matter of Rabbainu should endure for all generations — and he did not allow the Rabbi of Savran to marry Idel the daughter of Rabbainu. The Rabbi of Savran had wanted to take her as a wife and thereby call himself the successor of Rabbainu — which would have been a great harm. Therefore Moharan'as did not allow this — and this caused the Rabbi of Savran to dispute with Moharan'as with great intensity. And when the match was being discussed between them, Idel asked the Rabbi of Savran: "I have heard that you dispute with my father." He replied: "Not with your father — only with his disciple [Moharan'as], who said that your father is as great as Moshe Rabbainu." She replied to him: "What is the difference — Moshe Rabbainu brought down the Torah — and my father brings people to fulfill it!" And in the end the match was not completed, for Moharan'as did not agree.

And similarly it was at the great Shavuos gathering at Moharan'as's — on that Shavuos he witnessed an extraordinary spiritual awakening and Moharan'as himself said about that Shavuos that it was of extraordinary greatness.
